newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Anglo-Saxon banks keen on London OLO trade - paper.
newsitem.headline: Anglo-Saxon banks keen on London OLO trade - paper.

text.p: A number of Anglo-Saxon banks are interested in becoming primary dealers in Belgian state debt, but are asking to be allowed to operate from London, Belgian financial daily L'Echo said on Saturday.
A bank such as Salomon Brothers, which has no Brussels operations, could be interested in becoming a primary dealer, the paper said, quoting what it called a good source.

Fears have swept through the market in Belgian government bonds (OLOs) of a drain of activity away from Brussels to London since it emerged Deutsche Bank AG moved most of its OLO trading to the U.K. capital at the start of the year.
Deutsche is one of 15 primary dealers.
The German bank currently operates with one OLO trader in Brussels and calls from Belgian customers are often routed automatically to the London office, other dealers have said.
Current rules state that primary dealers have to be based in Belgium or Luxembourg.

L'Echo said there were also questions on the likely strategy of banks such as JP Morgan, currently a primary dealer with operations in Brussels, but with the bulk of its international bond activities in London.

The primary dealer system, set up in 1991, requires selected dealers to make a market in OLOs by continuously quoting bid and ask prices. They are allowed to take part in the Treasury's non-competitive OLO and Treasury bill auctions and enjoy a preferential relationship with the central bank.
